schema_front.purpose: Imported from FIBO (EDM Council, MIT), FND Agreements module, release master_2026Q3: a flat extraction contract for contracts — their parties, provisions, dates, and governing jurisdictions — scoped for the CUAD corpus of commercial contracts. FIBO definitions are carried verbatim where FIBO states them; boundary examples, and the definitions of the types FIBO grounds in OMG Commons (Organization, Jurisdiction, Date), are authored for this pack and recorded as authored in the import's scoping record (examples/fibo-import/fibo-contracts.scoping.json).

entity_inventory.definition: voluntary, deliberate agreement between competent parties to which the parties agree to be legally bound, and for which the parties provide valuable consideration

provisions: the termination clause (a provision of the contract, not the contract)
references: a prior agreement named only as superseded background in a recital, where the text does not present it as a contract in the corpus

entity_inventory.definition: individual human being, with consciousness of self

titles: the General Counsel (a role or title, not a named person)
collectives: the Supplier's employees (a group, not an individual)

entity_inventory.definition: element, such as an arrangement, provision, requirement, rule, specification, and standard that forms an integral part of an agreement
form_examples: a numbered section or clause of the contract

specific provisions: a clause whose whole content is a termination right (a TerminationProvision)
a clause that only defines a term (a ContractualDefinition)

entity_inventory.definition: provision specifying something that the contracting parties agree to, i.e., a promise or pledge made by one of the parties to perform some action or fulfill some duty

facts: a statement that something is the case (a Representation), not a promise that something will be done

entity_inventory.definition: contractual element that specifies the meaning of a term in a legal document, whose definition is substitutable for the term whenever it occurs in the body of that document
form_examples: a definition in the definitions section

mere uses: a later use of the defined term in an operative clause, without its definition

entity_inventory.definition: contractual element that specifies the circumstances under which the parties can dissolve their legal relationship and discontinue the fulfillment of their obligations under the contract

expiry: the contract simply reaching the end of its stated term, with no termination right exercised or granted

entity_inventory.definition: contract terms that specify the conditions under which a contract can be extended
form_examples: '…may extend the Term for two additional one-year periods…'

the period: the additional period itself (a duration, not the provision granting it)

entity_inventory.definition: contractual provision that outlines the requirements and responsibilities of one or both parties to reveal certain information to each other
form_examples: a confidentiality clause in a services agreement

definitions: the definition of Confidential Information itself (a ContractualDefinition)

entity_inventory.definition: provision indicating that notification is required prior to the occurrence of a relevant event
form_examples: 'All notices under this Agreement must be in writing to …'

sent notices: a termination notice actually sent under the provision (an act, not the provision requiring it)

entity_inventory.definition: contractual element that specifies the method of reducing credit, settlement and other risks by aggregating (combining) two or more obligations to achieve a reduced net obligation
form_examples: a close-out netting clause in a master agreement

payment terms: net-30 payment terms (a payment schedule, not the netting of obligations)

entity_inventory.definition: contractual element that is a statement of fact
form_examples: 'Supplier warrants that the Services will conform …'
a warranty clause with a stated warranty period

inducing statements: a statement of fact made to induce the contract, with no assurance or remedy attached (a Representation)

entity_inventory.definition: contractual element that is a statement made by a party to the contract, before or at the time of making the contract, in regard to some fact, circumstance, or state of affairs pertinent to the contract, which the counterparty(ies) rely on, or is influential in bringing about the contract
form_examples: 'Each party represents that it is duly organized …'

promises: a promise of future performance (a ContractualCommitment)

entity_inventory.definition: A named company, partnership, government agency, or other organized body that can enter into a contract as a party.
form_examples: a named LLC, partnership, or agency

units: the Legal Department of Acme (a unit of the party, not the contracting party itself)
defined terms: 'the Company' used as a defined term (extract the named organization it refers to)

entity_inventory.definition: A named state, country, or legal system whose law is stated to govern a contract or to host the resolution of its disputes.
form_examples: the laws of the State of New York

institutions: a named court (an institution seated in a jurisdiction, not the jurisdiction itself)

entity_inventory.definition: A specific calendar date stated in a contract — the day the contract or an obligation under it begins, is signed, renews, expires, or ends.

durations: thirty (30) days (a period, not a calendar date)
references: 'the date hereof' (a reference to a date, not a stated date)

relation_inventory.definition: indicates a party that has entered into a binding agreement, accepting and conceding obligations, responsibilities, and benefits as specified
boundary_examples: 'This Agreement is entered into by Acme Corp. and Beta LLC' states the relation for both; a company named only as a reference customer is not a contract party

relation_inventory.definition: identifies a party to a contract, typically not the contract principal
boundary_examples: the counterparty is the party on the other side of the principal; not every contract party is framed as a counterparty — a third-party beneficiary is not

relation_inventory.definition: identifies the main or principal party to a contract
boundary_examples: the principal is the main party the contract serves; an agent or signatory acting on the principal's behalf is not the principal party

relation_inventory.definition: identifies a party which is not signatory to the party but has some role in the overall context defined by the contract.
boundary_examples: a non-signatory named as having a role under the contract (e.g. an escrow agent); a signatory affiliate is a contract party, not a third party

relation_inventory.definition: party that receives some benefit or advantage or profits from something as specified in the agreement
boundary_examples: 'The Client's customers are third-party beneficiaries of this Section' states it; the party conferring the benefit is not its own beneficiary

relation_inventory.definition: indicates something that is a component of an agreement
boundary_examples: the provision is a component of this contract; a clause quoted from another contract for comparison is not an element of this one

relation_inventory.definition: indicates the date a contract, relationship, or policy comes into force
boundary_examples: the date the contract comes into force; the signing date is HasExecutionDate, and a date inside a provision is not the contract's effective date

relation_inventory.definition: indicates the date a contract has been signed by all the necessary parties
boundary_examples: the date the contract was signed by all necessary parties; one party's earlier signature date, where others signed later, is not the execution date

relation_inventory.definition: indicates a termination date that occurs prior to an explicit expiration date
boundary_examples: a termination date earlier than the stated expiration; the ordinary expiration date at the end of the term is not an early termination date

relation_inventory.definition: indicates the jurisdiction governing the contract, as agreed by all parties
boundary_examples: 'governed by the laws of the State of Delaware' states it; the place of signing or a party's home state does not, unless stated as governing

relation_inventory.definition: indicates a contract that was executed prior to and is replaced by this contract
boundary_examples: the prior contract is replaced and ceases to govern; an amendment that keeps the prior contract in force is not supersession

relation_inventory.definition: indicates the primary contract referenced by a subordinate agreement, such as a collateral agreement
boundary_examples: a collateral or subordinate agreement points at its primary contract; a schedule or exhibit is part of its own contract, not subordinate to it

relation_inventory.definition: indicates any subordinate agreement, such as a collateral agreement
boundary_examples: the same link as IsSubordinateTo, stated from the primary contract's side
